extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys) handling reissue applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating and prosecuting reissue patent applications (recapture, broadened claims, inventorship correction, drawings, and reissue oath/declaration requirements). Intended to direct examiner review and applicant practice under 35 U.S.C. 251 and related rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test for whether reissue claims are for the same invention
rubrics_metrics.description: The entire disclosure, not just the claim(s), is considered in determining what the patentee objectively intended as his or her invention. The proper test is an essentially factual inquiry confined to the objective intent manifested by the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims presented in a reissue application are considered to satisfy 35 U.S.C. 251 that the claims be 'for the invention disclosed in the original patent' where: (A) the claims presented in the reissue application are described in the original patent specification and enabled such that 35 U.S.C. 112 first paragraph is satisfied; and (B) nothing in the original patent specification indicates an intent not to claim the subject matter of the claims presented in the reissue application. Some disclosure (description and enablement) in the original patent should evidence that applicant intended to claim or considered the material now claimed to be his or her invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recapture prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue will not be granted to 'recapture' claimed subject matter which was surrendered in an application to obtain the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner and applicant must be guided by case law (Hester, Clement, Ball, etc.) showing that surrendered subject matter in original prosecution cannot be reclaimed by reissue. Rejections should be made under 35 U.S.C. 251 where recapture is present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-step test for recapture
rubrics_metrics.description: First determine whether and in what aspect the reissue claims are broader than the patent claims. Second, determine whether the broader aspects relate to surrendered subject matter by reviewing prosecution history for arguments/changes made to overcome prior art rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadening includes omission of a limitation. To determine surrender look to prosecution history (arguments, claim amendments) made in effort to overcome rejections (see Mentor, Clement, Ball). Each omitted or broadened limitation must be reviewed for relation to surrendered subject matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner review for presence of broadening
rubrics_metrics.description: In every reissue application, the examiner must first review each claim for the presence of broadening, as compared with the scope of the claims of the patent to be reissued.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reissue claim is broadened where some limitation of the patent claims is no longer required in the reissue claim. If a claim is in fact broadened, the examiner must next determine whether the broader aspects relate to previously surrendered subject matter. Identify omitted/broadened limitations and analyze each limitation of the patent claims omitted or broadened in the reissue claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for determining surrendered subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: If the limitation now being omitted or broadened was originally presented/argued/stated in the original application to make the claims allowable over a rejection or objection, the omitted limitation relates to subject matter previously surrendered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review original application prosecution history (rejections and applicant's arguments). An amendment added to obviate a rejection can establish surrender even without explicit argument. Examiner must look for specific, limitation-directed statements rather than boilerplate statements about claims generally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate arguments insufficient to show surrender
rubrics_metrics.description: General statements regarding the claims as a whole (e.g., 'the limitations of claims 1-7 distinguish the claims from the teachings of the prior art') are not sufficient by themselves to establish surrender and recapture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The argument that the claim limitation defined over the rejection must have been specific as to the limitation; a general 'boiler plate' sentence will not be sufficient to establish surrender.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument alone may effect surrender
rubrics_metrics.description: Surrender of claimed subject matter may occur by arguments made during the prosecution of the original patent application even where there was no claim change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following Hester, examiners should review prosecution history for persuasive applicant arguments that limit claim scope; argument-only surrender must be considered when deciding recapture rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recapture rule bars reclaiming previously cancelled subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: The recapture rule bars the patentee from acquiring through reissue claims that are, in all aspects, of the same scope as, or are broader in scope than, those claims canceled from the original application to obtain a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reissue claims are as broad as or broader than canceled original-application claims in aspects germane to prior art rejections, recapture applies (Ball Corp. and related cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue claims narrower in all aspects permitted (timing for certain broadenings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee is free to acquire, through reissue, claims that are narrower in scope in all aspects than claims canceled from the original application to obtain a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reissue claims are narrower than the canceled claims but broader than the issued patent claims, reissue must be sought within 2 years after the grant of the original patent. See MPEP § 1412.03 for broadening claims timing rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed broader and narrower aspects — avoid recapture if unrelated
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue claims that are broader in certain aspects and narrower in others vis-à-vis claims canceled from the original application may avoid the effect of the recapture rule if the claims are broader in a way that does not attempt to reclaim what was surrendered earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the broadening aspect relates to surrendered subject matter, determine whether any newly added narrowing limitation modifies the claim such that scope no longer results in recapture. If narrowing limits the claim to avoid recapture, explain reasons of record why no recapture exists; if not, reject for recapture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue to take advantage of 35 U.S.C. 103(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may file a reissue application to permit consideration of process claims which qualify for 35 U.S.C. 103(b) treatment if the patent is entitled to the benefit and the omission was an error without deceptive intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition of process claims will generally be considered a broadening of the invention and must be applied for within two years of the grant of the original patent. See Ex Parte Wikdahl and MPEP § 1412.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue for 'article' claims (computer-readable medium) — timing and broadening
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may file a reissue application to permit consideration of article of manufacture claims which are functional descriptive material stored on a computer-readable medium, where these article claims correspond to the patented process or machine claims; the error must have been without deceptive intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The addition of these 'article' claims will generally be considered a broadening of the invention and must be applied for within two years of the grant of the original patent. See Ex Parte Wikdahl and MPEP § 1412.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-and-examiner requirements when rejecting for recapture (¶14.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue claims which recapture surrendered subject matter should be rejected using form paragraph 14.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: explain specifics of why recapture exists, including identification of the omitted/broadened claim limitations that provide the 'broadening aspect' and where in the original application the narrowed claim scope was presented/argued to obviate a rejection/objection. See MPEP § 1412.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'broadened reissue claim'
rubrics_metrics.description: A broadened reissue claim is a claim which enlarges the scope of the claims of the patent, i.e., a claim which is greater in scope than each and every claim of the original patent. A claim of a reissue application enlarges the scope of the claims of the patent if it is broader in at least one respect, even though it may be narrower in other respects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim is broadened if it contains within its scope any conceivable product or process which would not have infringed the original patent claims. If any amended or newly added claim reads on something the original claims do not, it is broadened (Tillotson, In re Ruth, In re Rogoff).

rubrics_metrics.name: Addition of combination claims vs subcombination claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The addition of combination claims in a reissue application where only subcombination claims were present in the original patent could be a broadening of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze whether the added combination claim contains every limitation of the subcombination of any claim of the original patent. If the combination contains every limitation of the subcombination, infringement of the combination results in infringement of the subcombination and broadening may not exist; otherwise broadening exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of 35 U.S.C. 271(g) (broadening-indirect infringement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding a limitation to process claims (e.g., converting a claim to an intermediate into a claim to a final product) can provide an element of broadening because it may allow invocation of 35 U.S.C. 271(g) (liability for importation of products made by a patented process).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should be careful in chemical/process cases to check for this unique type of broadening: even an added step that appears narrowing may broaden practical protection by creating new infringers under 271(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claim enlarged but not a broadened reissue claim
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim that is broadened in a reissue as compared to its scope in the patent is not a broadened reissue claim if it is narrower than, or equal in scope to, any other claim which appears in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: dependent claim 2 may be broadened via reissue but if independent claim 1 is not broadened (and claim 2 must contain all limitations of claim 1), claim 2 is not a broadened reissue claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: When broadened claims may be presented — timing and intent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A broadened claim can be presented within two years from the grant of the original patent in a reissue application. A broadened claim can also be presented after two years if a broadening was indicated in the reissue application (or a parent reissue) within two years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reissue application filed on the 2-year anniversary date is timely. Cases: In re Graff, In re Fotland (oath/declaration indicating desire to seek broadened claims within two years required), In re Bennett (correction of declaration execution), In re Doll (timely indication in oath allows subsequent broadening). Examiners should check for improper presentation of broadened claims filed outside the two-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue as vehicle to correct inventorship vs certificate of correction
rubrics_metrics.description: Reissue may correct misjoinder of inventors where 35 U.S.C. 256 is inadequate. However, correction of inventorship should be effected under 35 U.S.C. 256 and 37 CFR 1.324 by filing a request for a certificate of correction if the only change is inventorship and all parties agree and issue is uncontested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where 35 U.S.C. 256/1.324 do not apply, a reissue application is appropriate to correct inventorship. Reissue is a vehicle for correcting inventorship under 35 U.S.C. 251; see case law (Ex parte Scudder, A.F. Stoddard & Co. v. Dann).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration content and signature rules for inventorship correction
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath or declaration must state that the applicant believes the original patent to be wholly or partly inoperative or invalid through error in inventorship and that such error arose without deceptive intention; it must comply with 37 CFR 1.175 and 1.63.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reissue does not seek to enlarge claims, the reissue oath may be made and sworn to by the assignee of the entire interest (37 CFR 1.172). If a reissue to correct inventorship also changes claims to enlarge scope, inventors' signatures are required; if an inventor refuses, a petition under 37 CFR 1.47 may be used. Petitions under 1.48 or 1.324 should not be used in a reissue application; if filed, they should be dismissed and fees refunded, and material considered under 1.175 if compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and amendment of drawings in reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings upon which the original patent was issued may be used in reissue applications if no changes are to be made. Amendments to drawings are restricted and governed by 37 CFR 1.121(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using original drawings, submit a temporary drawing copy (printed drawings or photoprint) on filing. Amendments: amending (physically altering) original patent drawing sheets is not permitted; changes must be by filing new sheet(s) with amended figures identified as 'amended' and added figures as 'new'. A sketch in permanent ink showing proposed changes in red must be filed for examiner approval; examiner must inspect for new matter and conformity to specification. Procedures for canceling/replacing sheets, inserting new sheets, and notifying applicant if change request is not approved are specified. Requests to alter original drawing sheets should be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirement of reissue oath/declaration (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath or declaration, in addition to complying with § 1.63, must state that the applicant believes the original patent to be wholly or partly inoperative or invalid by reason of a defective specification or drawing, or by reason of the patentee claiming more or less than the patentee had the right to claim, stating at least one error relied upon as the basis for reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a statutory and regulatory content requirement for a reissue filing under 37 CFR 1.175; the applicant must identify at least one error being relied upon.
